about: Nicolas-Jay is a partnership between Jean-Nicolas Méo, who runs the celebrated Domaine Méo-Camuzet in Vosne-Romanée, and Jay Boberg, a former music-industry executive. Their friendship goes back decades, and their first Oregon vintage was 2014, shortly after they bought the Bishop Creek vineyard in the Yamhill-Carlton district. In 2019 they bought a 53-acre estate in the Dundee Hills, where a converted barn now holds the winery, cellars and tasting room, and the land is farmed organically with no tilling.

Most of the world’s vines are grafted onto American rootstock to resist phylloxera. This cuvée comes only from vines on their own roots, many more than forty years old, in three organic or biodynamic sites: Bishop Creek (planted 1987), Nysa (1990) and Hyland (1971), one of McMinnville’s oldest vineyards. As in Burgundy, the fruit is destemmed, cold-soaked for about four days and fermented with native yeasts. The 2022 was aged with about half new French oak and bottled unfined and unfiltered. Only 413 cases were made.

Vinous’s Eric Guido found a spice-box bouquet, ripe red berries and a saline, mineral edge, and Jamie Goode noted sweet cherry and plum with a fine, grainy structure. Others describe a savoury side of olive, forest floor and cocoa over dark berry fruit, a wine that is dark for Pinot Noir yet light on its feet.
facts: Destemmed, native-yeast fermentation; unfined and unfiltered
